title: cafaye trace signal
description: What a cafaye span is permitted to carry. The per-signal attribute allowlist for traces, and the shape of a span record that exports it. Three rules are encoded here rather than described in a README, because a rule that is not in schemas/ is not a cafaye rule (AGENTS.md): span names follow span-naming.schema.json, the attribute set is closed with additionalProperties: false so an attribute nobody thought about is a failure rather than a silent export, and no allowlisted name contains a word that names content. That last one is muse's canary promoted to a spec-level assertion — muse/tests/test_trace_propagation.py asserts the same property of muse's ALLOWED_SPAN_ATTRIBUTES end to end through a real request, and a real leak arrives as a well-meaning `muse.prompt` added in six months, not as an attacker. `error.message` is deliberately absent: a provider's content-policy rejection quotes the offending content back, so the message is a prompt by another route. `error.type` is the grouping key, a low-cardinality class. See docs/observability.md.

name.description: Byte-identical to the pattern in span-naming.schema.json, which tests/test_specs.py asserts. A span name the traces schema accepts and the naming schema does not is a name core contradicts itself about.

kind.description: The OpenTelemetry span kind. A property of the span, never part of its name — a name that encodes the kind is a name that has to change when the relationship does.

attributes.description: The span's attributes, drawn from the trace allowlist. `additionalProperties: false` inside the allowlist itself, so a span carrying an attribute core has never heard of is rejected at the collector and in a service's own contract test rather than exported and stored.

resource.description: Attributes attached once per process rather than per span — service identity, version, deployment. They are exempt from the metric cardinality cap, which is why identity belongs here and not on a measurement. See metrics.schema.json.

status.description: The OpenTelemetry span status. `code` is an enum rather than a string so a status cannot be invented per service; a service with a status core does not know about is a dashboard that silently misses it.

code.description: The OTel status code. `error` is a claim, and it obliges the span to carry `error.type`.

message.description: A short static string for a human, such as `provider auth rejected`. Never an exception message, never a stack trace, never anything a caller or a vendor supplied: see the redaction boundary in redaction.schema.json.

links.description: Links to causally related spans, for the case a parent-child edge cannot express (a batch job whose items share no span). Bounded at 16, which is the OTel default link limit — an unbounded link list is a span whose size is a function of its data.

spanName.description: Byte-identical to `$defs/spanName` in span-naming.schema.json. Duplicated rather than `$ref`d because a service's SDK setup reads this file alone; a cross-file ref would make the file un-loadable without a resolver, and core's whole premise is that a service compiles against these files by path.

tracesAttributes.description: The complete set of attribute names a cafaye span may carry. Anything not listed is not emitted — default-deny, so an attribute added in a hurry is dropped rather than shipped. The dotted OpenTelemetry semantic-convention names are used for facts the ecosystem already has a name for, so a span exported to a backend nobody at cafaye has heard of is still readable. Each entry's `description` says what the attribute is a fact ABOUT, because the test that keeps content out is a test about names.

http.request.method.description: The HTTP method. Bounded by the enum, which is what makes it a legal measurement attribute too.

http.response.status_code.description: The response status. Bounded to 500 values. Note the metrics signal carries the *class* rather than the code — see metrics.schema.json.

http.route.description: The ROUTE TEMPLATE (`/v1/users/{id}`), never the concrete path. This is the distinction the whole attribute rule turns on: a template has one value per endpoint, a concrete path has one per request. `url.path` and `url.full` are not on the list for that reason, and neither is any query string — a query string is caller text by another name.

db.system.description: The database product. Four values; this is what a bounded dimension looks like.

db.operation.description: The database operation. A closed vocabulary of verbs rather than the statement text, which is caller-influenced and would be a leak on the SQL-injection path.

messaging.system.description: The transport. `postgres-outbox` is the fleet default (PLAN.md §7b: drain your own outbox, do not add a broker), so a span that crosses a service boundary says so by name.

messaging.operation.description: What the span did to the message. The delivery attempt count belongs here as a bounded integer, never the message body.

otel.status_code.description: The OTel status, mirrored as an attribute so a log-indexed query can filter on it. The span's own `status.code` is the field of record.

error.type.description: The low-cardinality error CLASS — the grouping key for every error in the fleet, and the reason there is one place to see all errors rather than a wall of ungrouped text (PLAN.md §7b). snake_case, bounded to 64 characters, constrained to a class shape. Never a message, never a stack trace, never an interpolated value: a free string in this field is a cardinality bomb on the metrics side and an ungroupable wall of text on the traces side. The vocabulary is bounded because the two halves of that failure are the same failure — see D14 in DECISIONS.md for the granularity call and what a consumer can and cannot aggregate on.

resource.description: Attributes attached once per process. Exempt from the 2000-combination metric cap and preserved on the overflow point, which is the correct home for identity — see metrics.schema.json for why that matters, and for why the same value on a measurement is the failure this whole spec exists to prevent.

tenant_id.description: The tenant, here and never on a measurement. Unbounded as a dimension, exempt as a resource.

account_id.description: The account, same reasoning as tenant_id.
